title: Sequoia Initiative POC Weekly Pulse - Cost & Throughput
summary: Weekly POC checkpoint focused on tokens-per-dollar and throughput tradeoffs. Reviewed pilot numbers since last week (tokens/sec per dollar, caching delta, batch sizing experiments). Agreed to run a 30-min dedicated benchmark with prefetched prefix cache and larger batch windows; Redwood to share benchmark script, updated pricing for dedicated lanes, and a short spreadsheet with projected unit econ across three traffic shapes.
action_items: Maya: Share benchmark script (secure link) and sample prompt set - due 2026-07-16
Liam: Provision a dedicated test pool config and notes on expected perf variance - due 2026-07-17
Ravi: Provide 3 representative traffic traces (avg/peak/p95) and the auth for sandbox - due 2026-07-15
next_steps: Redwood to run 30-min dedicated run with cache warmup and send raw logs + token accounting
Customer to confirm SLA targets (p95 latency targets) and whether VPC test required for dedicated benchmark
Schedule call next Friday 2026-07-17 to review benchmark outputs and pricing scenarios
transcript:
Meeting start: 2026-07-13 15:00 UTC - Duration approx 38m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Sequoia Eng Lead), Aisha Noor (Data Eng), Jordan Lee (PM), Priya Singh (Ops)

00:00 Speaker 1: hey everybody, thanks for hopping on, um well do a quick pulse on the pilot econ and next steps. maya over to you.
00:22 Maya Chen (AE): thanks, yeah quick agenda, tokens per dollar, caching numbers from last 48 hours, batch tuning notes, and then next step benchmark. call should be ~30-40 minutes.
00:38 Ravi Patel: cool, quick context, were able to run more tests this week, we captured a traffic shape extracted from the prod-like harness, about 320 reqs/minute peak, avg 140, p95 spiky.
00:58 Liam Ortiz (SE): perfect, so we ran two main configs: hosted baseline (gpt-ish open model patch) and a quantized dedicated pool with 16k context, we saw tokens/sec per dollar delta of about 2.1x in favor of dedicated after caching.
01:18 Aisha Noor: when you say caching, is that prefix cache or the KV cache? i remember last time we had the K-V cash not warming correctly.
01:30 Liam Ortiz (SE): yeah sorry, prefix / KV cache — the test used prefix caching for repeated system prompts and KV cache warmup for conversational flows. we observed ~28% token cost savings in the conversational replay after warmup. note: warmup was simulated with 10K tokens prefix warms.
01:52 Jordan Lee (PM): 28% is great, but what's the latency impact? our p95 must stay under 450ms for tokens streaming.
02:05 Liam Ortiz (SE): on hosted baseline p95 was ~380ms, dedicated (with larger batch windows) p95 moved to ~520ms at batch size 24, but if we reduce batch to 8, p95 is ~410ms and tokens/sec/$ drops by ~12%. tradeoff.
02:32 Ravi Patel: can you repeat that with numbers? tokens per dollar - baseline to dedicated?
02:40 Maya Chen (AE): sure. baseline hosted: ~0.00045 tokens per USD-second (this is shorthand), dedicated without cache: ~0.00095, dedicated with cache: ~0.0020. those are rough from last night's run.
03:03 Priya Singh (Ops): the accounting unit here is a little confusing, can you add tokens/sec per dollar as tokens per second divided by cost per second?
03:13 Liam Ortiz (SE): yes i can send the spreadsheet, it's basically tokens/sec ÷ $/sec. the quick takeaway — cache multiplies effective tokens handled per dollar by reducing repeated compute.
03:28 Speaker 6: (unintelligible)
03:36 Aisha Noor: any notes on prompt engineering? some of our prompts have long instruction prefixes, which inflates cost before caching helps.
03:46 Maya Chen (AE): good point — our suggestion was to move static instructions into a system prompt that gets K-V cached, that reduces tokens for each user request. we noted ~9-11% further savings in one of the mini-experiments.
04:05 Jordan Lee (PM): were also tracking quality regression, last week you noted a small drop when swapping quantized model - are we confident quality remains within our thresholds?
04:17 Liam Ortiz (SE): we ran the eval harness on the 200 prompt set; differences were within noise for 87% of cases, 6% showed mild wording variance, 7% edge cases. we flagged 12 prompts for further inspection.
04:36 Ravi Patel: okay thanks. next, on batching — you said larger batch sizes help tokens/sec but hurt latency. can you show the breakpoints?
04:47 Liam Ortiz (SE): yep, breakpoints we measured: batch=4 gives best p95 ~390ms but lower throughput; batch=8 p95 ~410ms, throughput up ~18% vs batch4; batch=16 p95 ~480ms throughput +36%; batch=24 p95 ~520ms throughput +48%. for the quantized pipeline, the curve is similar but absolute latency slightly higher.
05:18 Priya Singh (Ops): that maps to our q95 SLOs — wed prefer p95 <450 so maybe batch=12 is a compromise but we don't have that data point. can you run batch=12?
05:29 Liam Ortiz (SE): yes we can add batch=12 in the follow-up run.
05:35 Maya Chen (AE): also worth calling out autoscaling effects; when you run sustained peak at 320 reqs/min, autoscaler will provision more pods/GPUs causing jitter during scale events. we recommend ramp tests.
05:50 Aisha Noor: are autoscale events visible in the logs? we need audit-able events for compliance.
05:56 Liam Ortiz (SE): yes audit logs include scale up/down events in the private control plane; for hosted we can surface a matching alert. we also log per-token and per-request metadata for debugging.
06:12 Jordan Lee (PM): security question — do you have SOC2 and can we get a whitepaper? also KMS integration for key rotation?
06:22 Maya Chen (AE): Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; we will share the SOC2 summary and the KMS integration guide. key rotation and envelope encryption supported; in private deployment we integrate with customer KMS.
06:33 Ravi Patel: great. on the pricing side — if we moved to a dedicated reserved pool what are the delta price points? we need numbers to feed finance.
06:43 Maya Chen (AE): we'll provide a three-scenario pricing: hosted on-demand, burst-dedicated, and reserved monthly commit. for the pilot, we can show per-token and per-hour numbers and the projected unit econ for your traffic shapes.
06:56 Priya Singh (Ops): can you show us the spreadsheet with the math?
07:02 Maya Chen (AE): yes, we'll attach it; includes tokens/sec/$ and total cost for 3 traffic patterns you provided.
07:12 Ravi Patel: quick question on VPC/private test. to emulate our production network, would you need us to open ports or set up a VPN?
07:20 Liam Ortiz (SE): for the private test we have two options: temporary secure peering or run an on-prem package. for the dedicated benchmark we can run within Redwood's hosted testbed if you'd prefer — only requirement is sample traces and prompt set. if you want VPC, we'll need network details.
07:38 Jordan Lee (PM): let's start without VPC to get raw numbers, then plan a VPC run if dedicated looks promising.
07:46 Aisha Noor: the cache warmup pattern you used — can you describe exactly how you seeded it? we want to replicate on our side.
07:53 Liam Ortiz (SE): we prepopulated the prefix cache with 10K tokens using the same system prompts, then replayed 5K conversational flows where the initial turns hit the cache. we'll send the script.
08:10 Maya Chen (AE): small note — the cache hit rate for those runs was about 62%, after 30 minutes sustained traffic it rose to ~71% in our sim. your real traffic shape might change that.
08:23 Ravi Patel: that 71% number is optimistic for our user base, maybe we'll be 45-55% since we have many unique prefixes.
08:31 Liam Ortiz (SE): understood — that's why we asked for your traces. even at 50% cache the delta is meaningful; our sensitivity table shows 50% cache yields ~18-20% cost savings vs 0% cache.
08:46 Priya Singh (Ops): curious — are you measuring tokens vs prompt tokens only or including system prompt length cost?
08:53 Liam Ortiz (SE): it's total tokens billed. the spreadsheet breaks out static vs dynamic so you can see how much static instructions add.
09:05 Jordan Lee (PM): any blockers on Redwoods side for running a 30-minute dedicated test at scale?
09:12 Maya Chen (AE): none, just need your traces and greenlight on whether to include VPC test. we'll provision the dedicated pool for a short window.
09:22 Ravi Patel: ok we'll deliver traces and confirm schedule by Friday.
09:28 Speaker 3: (background)
09:34 Liam Ortiz (SE): quick note on quality monitoring — we recommend running the evaluation suite pre/post every change; we'll attach the eval results from the quantized run and highlight the 12 prompts.
09:46 Aisha Noor: please add exact deltas per prompt, not just aggregate.
09:50 Liam Ortiz (SE): will do.
09:55 Maya Chen (AE): anything else on tokens/sec/$?
10:00 Ravi Patel: yeah — can you show the worst-case dollar per 1M tokens number? finance wants that for risk modeling.
10:07 Maya Chen (AE): we have a worst-case hosted on-demand of approx $480 per M tokens (this includes some buffer), dedicated optimized with caching went down to ~ $98 per M tokens in our test matrix. again depends on context lengths and cache hit rate.
10:26 Priya Singh (Ops): that's a big spread. we'll need the assumptions spelled out in the spreadsheet.
10:32 Maya Chen (AE): absolutely, assumptions will be line-itemed.
10:36 Jordan Lee (PM): for the next run, can we include a burst pattern test: 5 min steady, 2 min spike x3. we want to see scale latency.
10:45 Liam Ortiz (SE): yes we can add that. we'll also capture autoscale logs and pod spin-up times.
10:52 Ravi Patel: one more thing — competitor question, anthro/anthropic performance numbers we've seen are a bit lower cost but our data shows more variability — will you include comparative numbers?
11:03 Maya Chen (AE): we can include public benchmark references, but we'll be explicit about differences in prompt sets and context windows.
11:12 Aisha Noor: timeline — when do you expect results?
11:15 Maya Chen (AE): we can run the dedicated 30-min benchmark early next week, share logs same day, then quick follow-up call Friday. so results by 2026-07-17 EOD likely.
11:26 Ravi Patel: sounds good. action items recap?
11:30 Maya Chen (AE): recap: Maya share script & spreadsheet; Liam add batch=12 and burst pattern, provision dedicated run; Ravi provide traces and auth; we'll reconvene next Friday.
11:45 Jordan Lee (PM): thanks all.
11:50 Meeting end.
